item.text: There isn’t an existing app framework here, so I’m making this a small Node server with a plain HTML/CSS/JS interface. The server will expose book endpoints and save each change to a local JSON file, while each book gets its own shareable URL.

The core flow is in place: add a title, author, and optional notes; see reading and finished lists; open a book’s own URL; and mark it finished. I’m doing a final pass on the labels and edge handling so the app describes its local JSON storage accurately.

item.text:
Built a small reading journal with no accounts or database.

- `npm start` launches the app at `http://localhost:3000`.
- The shelf shows currently reading and finished books. Add books with a title, author, and optional notes, then mark them finished.
- Each book has its own `/books/:id` page with a share button.
- Books persist in [books.json](/workspace/data/books.json). The server creates the file if it’s missing.
- The interface and server are in [public/app.js](/workspace/public/app.js), [public/styles.css](/workspace/public/styles.css), and [server.js](/workspace/server.js).

I didn’t run a test suite.
